title: Low-dose oral misoprostol for induction of labour.
abstract: Oral misoprostol is a common labour induction method. This review is restricted to lower doses (initially ≤ 50 µg), as higher doses pose unacceptably high risks of uterine hyperstimulation. To assess the benefits and harms of low-dose oral misoprostol for labour induction in women with a viable fetus in the third trimester of pregnancy, compared with other methods of labour induction. We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO ICTRP, and checked reference lists…

title: Regimens of vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy.
abstract: Vitamin D deficiency is common in pregnancy and has been associated with adverse health outcomes for the mother and infant, including pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and low birthweight. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a vitamin D intake of 200 international units (IU) per day during pregnancy. Vitamin D supplementation is recommended for women with suspected vitamin D deficiency, but it is not universally recommended. The effects of different doses (regimens)…

title: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) for treating advanced epithelial ovarian cancer.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the eighth most common cancer in women worldwide. Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the most common type; three-quarters of cases present with advanced disease (stage III or IV). Treatment consists of combinations of surgery and chemotherapy. Although initial responses to chemotherapy are good, most women with advanced disease relapse. Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) prevent cancer cells from repairing DNA damage, especially in those with breast cancer suscepti…

title: Chest physiotherapy for pneumonia in children.
abstract: Pneumonia is the single largest infectious cause of death in children aged under five years and remains a relevant cause of illness and death amongst older children and adolescents worldwide. Most pneumonia-related deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries, where access to healthcare resources, diagnostic services, and supportive treatments may be more limited than in high-income settings. Chest physiotherapy is widely used as adjuvant treatment for pneumonia. Physiotherapy is thought to…

title: Levothyroxine for subclinical hypothyroidism.
abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To evaluate the benefits and harms of levothyroxine for adults with subclinical hypothyroidism, compared with placebo or no treatment.

title: Living evidence map of the global climate and health literature.
abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (flexible). The objectives are as follows: The objectives of this living evidence map are to: systematically map the breadth, scope, and characteristics of the global literature on the relationship of climate change, climate variability, weather, climate-forcing agents, and fossil fuels with human health and well-being; enable ongoing, up-to-date access to the evolving evidence base through a living approach (encompassing content currency and adjustment o…

title: Levodopa or dopamine agonists for enhancing motor function after stroke.
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. There is a lack of evidence regarding pharmacological enhancement of stroke recovery with dopamine agonists or levodopa, in particular in terms of motor deficits. To assess the effects of dopaminergic agents, defined as levodopa or dopamine agonists, on improving motor function after stroke. We conducted an extensive database search on the Cochrane Stroke Group trials register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Science Ci…

title: Maternity versus non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy.
abstract: Substantial uncertainty exists regarding how healthcare system factors, especially care setting types, affect the uptake and implementation of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy screening in practice. Evidence suggests that the care environment may influence diagnostic processes. To assess the effectiveness of maternity and non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus or diabetes in pregnancy. We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cumulative…

title: Ergonomic interventions for treating work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder in adults.
abstract: Work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) are disorders that develop as a result of repetitive movements, awkward postures or external forces (e.g. vibrating tools), and significantly affect the working population globally. Ergonomic interventions (which aim to enhance efficiency and comfort in the working environment) can be used to manage CANS. This review is based on a new protocol but updates part of a 2013 Cochrane review. To assess the effectiveness of ergonomic intervent…

title: Music-based interventions for people with kidney failure undergoing haemodialysis.
abstract: People receiving haemodialysis for kidney failure experience substantial symptom burden, including anxiety, depression, and pain, which adversely affect physical function and quality of life. Music-based interventions are increasingly used as non-pharmacological strategies to address these symptoms; however, their effectiveness and the certainty of the evidence remain unclear. An updated systematic review of recent randomised controlled trials (RCTs) is therefore warranted. To assess the effects…
